lead.headline: Beefy Boys Go Perfect: 164.2 and a Rout
lead.deck: The Big Beefy Boys posted the highest score of the season with a lineup that could not have been improved by a single point.
paragraphs: {T8} scored 164.2 in week 5, the best total anyone has posted this season. The old mark was 161.28, shared by Kazakhstan and the Doughboys. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 37.7, Jaylen Warren 36.8 on a 17.6 projection, Josh Allen 30.5 and George Pickens 28.0 from the flex. That is 133.0 points from four players.

The best possible lineup from that roster also scored 164.2. Deebo Samuel Sr. started for 2.5 and Mark Andrews for 4.8, and both were still the right call: David Montgomery's 1.1 was the best score on the bench. A week ago this same team lost by 4.16 with 46 points sitting there.

Across the field, {T6} set a perfect lineup too. It scored 104.6, and so did its best possible lineup. Chase Brown returned 7.0 on a 17.4 projection and Romeo Doubs 2.6 on 12.2. Two perfect lineups produced the largest margin of the week, 59.6 points.

Beefy is 4–1 and went 11–0 in this week's all-play, which counts a team's record as if it played everyone every week. It now leads the league in points for at 671.96, 0.88 ahead of {S12}. Both teams are 4–1 with a 41–14 all-play record.

sidebar.title: Best Game of the Week: Benched
sidebar.text: {T10} left Drake Maye on the bench, and he scored 39.46, more than any starter in the league. The projections favored Jared Goff, 19.4 to 18.5, and Goff scored 28.94. Pink Pony won by 18.34 anyway.

sidebar.title: Same Points, Two Wins Apart
sidebar.text: {S2} has scored 642.42 and is 4–1. {S11} has scored 641.08 and is 2–3. Detroit has allowed 456.04, the fewest in the league; Kazakhstan has allowed 689.48, the most. This week Detroit won with 99.14, a score that beat one team. It was the team they played.

12-9.headline: Two Zeros, Still a Win
12-9.text: Bucky Irving scored 31.5 from the flex and Joe Burrow 24.6. {S12} won while starting the Chiefs D/ST and Harrison Butker, both projected for zero. {S9} got 32.3 from Christian Watson and 32.26 from Jayden Daniels, but RJ Harvey started for 0.7 with Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 14.2 on the bench. Their best lineup, 127.76, would have won.

7-5.headline: The Winning Lineup Sat on the Bench
7-5.text: Matthew Stafford scored 27.32, Jaxon Smith-Njigba 22.8, and the 49ers D/ST 20 on a 4.9 projection. {S5} started Tyler Shough at quarterback for -0.16 while Sam Darnold scored 8.3 on the bench, and CeeDee Lamb for 2.9 over Emeka Egbuka's 17.2. Their best lineup, 142.8, would have won.

10-4.headline: Pony Wins Again; Perfect Isn't Enough
10-4.text: Malik Nabers scored 29.1 and Jared Goff 28.94 as {S10} posted its best score of the season, 24.68 above the old high. {S4} left nothing on the bench and still lost by 18.34. Kenyon Sadiq scored 0.3 at tight end and Bijan Robinson 15.8 on a 22.2 projection.

2-3.headline: Doughboys' Worst Week Is Still a Win
2-3.text: {S2} scored a season-low 99.14 and won by 21.94, its fourth straight win. Jeremiyah Love started for 2.2 while MarShawn Lloyd scored 16.7 on the bench. {S3} started Josh Jacobs and Jaxson Dart, both projected for zero, for the second week running. Its best lineup, 93.8, would still have lost.

1-11.headline: Chimpanzini Snaps Out of It
1-11.text: Isaiah Likely scored 32.4 on a 12.9 projection, the biggest beat in the league, and Parker Washington added 30.4. New pickups Jacoby Brissett (25.28) and Will Reichard (16) both delivered. {S11} got 37.7 from Puka Nacua, but 5.3 from DK Metcalf and 1 from the Steelers D/ST.

8-6.headline: See Page One
8-6.text: Gibbs 37.7, Warren 36.8, Allen 30.5, Pickens 28.0. For {S6}, Sam LaPorta scored 19.8 and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked for 17.

honor.title: Big Beefy Boys
honor.text: Nathan LaWarre left 0.00 points on the bench while scoring the season's highest total. Two other teams also went perfect; neither won. Last week this lineup left 46 points on the bench in a 4-point loss.

blotter.title: Quarterback below zero
blotter.text: Started Tyler Shough for -0.16 with Sam Darnold's 8.3 on the bench, and CeeDee Lamb's 2.9 over Emeka Egbuka's 17.2. Lost by 14.18 with 22.76 on the bench.

blotter.title: Lost by 12.84, benched 25.2
blotter.text: RJ Harvey started for 0.7 while Jacory Croskey-Merritt scored 14.2 on the bench. Khalil Shakir's 11.0 sat too. The best lineup would have won by 3.06.

blotter.title: Repeat offender
blotter.text: Josh Jacobs and Jaxson Dart, projected for zero, started for the second straight week. Bo Nix (7.92) and Michael Wilson (7.28) watched from the bench again.

blotter.title: Kicking with no kicker
blotter.text: Started the Chiefs D/ST and Harrison Butker, both projected for zero. Both scored zero. Won by 12.84, so nobody is pressing charges.

blotter.title: Possession of the week's best game
blotter.text: Drake Maye scored 39.46 on the bench, the most by any player in the league. Released on account of the win.

ads.title: Wanted: a quarterback
ads.text: Released Dontayvion Wicks. Signed Jacoby Brissett, who started and scored 25.28 in a 31-point win.

ads.title: Kicker, new in box
ads.text: Out: Jason Myers. In: Will Reichard, who kicked for 16 in his first start.

ads.text: Emanuel Wilson in off waivers for Rico Dowdle. Started and scored 13.2 in a win.

ads.text: Bengals D/ST in, Cowboys D/ST out. Nine points in an 18-point win.
